claims.text: Reported GBP figures print as exactly the pence they were computed from, so M2 and M19-M25 add up to M17 as printed. _gbp is now p / 100 (an int quotient, correctly rounded) and refuses any figure of MAX_PENCE = 10**15 pence or more. Amounts and balances at or above that limit are refused with AmountError before any figure is computed. Below the limit a figure has at most 15 significant digits, so a binary float holds it and prints it back exactly. The reviewer's case (a £100000000000000.00 credit and a £0.01 credit) is refused, naming L1.

The lowest balance (M5) and overdrawn days (M6) are now computed in integer pence. balance_pence converts each line's balance once. end_of_day_balances returns pence. M5 reports the pence of the lowest balance through _gbp.

cma run's refusals escape Rich markup. A line id such as [red] now shows in the exit-6 reconciliation refusal. The exit-2 refusals (StatementError, PolicyError, RulesetError, AmountError) are escaped the same way.
MCP compute_metrics refuses unreconciled buckets with a ReconciliationError, which is a ValueError subclass. The error names the difference in pence and the line id. A contracts test now proves this.

The P1, P2 (money-in sums M2, M17-M25) and P6 invariants pass on every synthetic case and on 40 random statements under each of v1 and v2. They also pass on 300 random large-amount cases read back as printed decimals.

notes: Stop condition: two of verify-127's majors cannot be fixed without changing a shared contract the design did not list. The owner must decide how far P2 reaches. (1) P2 reads 'for any sum figure, the signed amounts of its evidence lines SHALL total the figure'. M8, M11, M12 and M14 have been positive figures for money out since before this change, so their evidence's signed total is the figure negated. Meeting P2 literally changes their values, which R10 ('ids, units and values of M1 to M16 unchanged') and P7's frozen baseline forbid, and it would ripple into policy thresholds, the guard and the memo template. (2) M9 caps a round-trip offset. Citing only the lines whose amounts it counts leaves M9's value unchanged but changes its evidence. The frozen P7 baseline pins M1-M16 evidence hashes, so I built this change, saw two P7 tests fail on the CARD ACQUIRER SETTLEMENT fixture, and reverted it. Suggested resolutions: (a) P2 covers the money-in buckets, M17, M18 and the monthly cells. Its 'Validates' line names R1, R11, R16 and R55, not the legacy obligations figures. M8/M11/M12/M14 are read as magnitudes of money out, and M9 as a net. Or (b) the owner approves changing those M1-M16 values or evidence, and the P7 baseline is rebuilt with that listed as the change R10 allows. This change's P2 test checks M2 and M17-M25 exactly, checks the four outflow figures as negated sums, and leaves out M9, with comments saying so. AmountError is a new ValueError subclass in metrics. cma run reports it as 'Refused.' with exit 2, and MCP raises it as a ValueError. The limit of 10**15 pence (£10 trillion per line, balance or figure) sits far above any real statement. I did not commit: the runner records the commit.
